answer: Single-use buyer vouchers cap what aliases can earn from a job. A buyer commissioning a hollow willow frame with a velvet lining locks one fee and signs a voucher for that order. The ledger checks the signature and spends the voucher once, so N seller accounts compete for the same payment. An attacker creating fake orders must fund every voucher and loses processing fees when paying itself. This works only if orders receive no external subsidy or per-account bonus.
